links.title: Chapter 4: Functions - the lecture deck for this chapter
links.why: The slides this chapter is taught from (deck 3.0.0): 46 numbered slides, short speaker notes, every code example also in the Chapter code tab of this page, in slide order.

links.title: 4. More Control Flow Tools
links.why: The tutorial's walk through def, default values, keyword arguments, and a function that returns None when it has no return.

links.title: PEP 570 – Python Positional-Only Parameters
links.why: Introduces the / separator: every parameter to its left can only be passed by position.

links.title: PEP 3102 – Keyword-Only Arguments
links.why: Explains arguments that can only be supplied by keyword, declared after a bare star in the parameter list.

links.title: 8. Compound statements — function definitions
links.why: The formal grammar of def, including default values evaluated once at definition time and parameter annotations.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the return statement
links.why: States that return leaves the call with the given value, or None when no expression is given.

links.title: Built-in Constants
links.why: Defines None as the absence of a value and the only instance of NoneType.

links.title: traceback — Print or retrieve a stack traceback
links.why: Functions such as print_stack and extract_stack that print or retrieve the current call stack and its frames.

links.title: 9. Classes — Python scopes and namespaces
links.why: Defines namespaces and scopes and shows how the global and nonlocal statements change where a name is bound.

links.title: 4. Execution model
links.why: Precise rules for binding and resolving names, including the UnboundLocalError raised for a local used before assignment.

links.title: 8. Errors and Exceptions
links.why: Covers try and except, several except clauses for different exception types, raising exceptions, and the built-in ones.

links.title: PEP 3107 – Function Annotations
links.why: The original proposal for annotating parameters and return values, stored in the __annotations__ attribute.

links.title: PEP 649 – Deferred Evaluation Of Annotations Using Descriptors
links.why: Describes delaying evaluation of annotation expressions until they are examined, the mechanism behind Python 3.14 annotations.

links.title: PEP 8 – Style Guide for Python Code
links.why: The official conventions for naming functions and formatting function annotations.

links.title: Python Tutor
links.why: Run code in the browser and step through it line by line with stack frames and variables drawn.

links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition - Chapter 4: Functions
links.why: The textbook chapter this course chapter follows, free to read online.

links.title: Programming FAQ - why am I getting an UnboundLocalError
links.why: The FAQ explains why reading a name before assigning it in the same function fails (deck slide 28).

links.title: inspect - Inspect live objects
links.why: Reference for inspect.stack and frame objects, which the call-stack examples of the deck use.

links.title: What's New In Python 3.14
links.why: Lists deferred annotations and the except clause without parentheses (deck slides 36 and 43).

links.title: PEP 758 - Allow except and except* expressions without parentheses
links.why: The proposal behind the Python 3.14 story of the deck: authors, dates and the rule.

links.title: David Wheeler (computer scientist) - Wikipedia
links.why: Who invented the closed subroutine on EDSAC in Cambridge (deck story, slide 8).

links.title: Collatz conjecture - Wikipedia
links.why: The unsolved 1937 problem behind the practice program (deck story, slide 42).
